Subject: Private VPC deployment — request for annotated topology and control/data split

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our security and infra teams asked for a single-sheet annotated topology showing the proposed control plane / data plane demarcation for the Private VPC deployment plus notes on egress controls and audit log paths.

We've sketched high-level requirements in the attached Excel (northstar_network_requirements.xlsx) — key asks are:
- Customer-managed KMS integration for tenant keys
- Hardened egress (deny-by-default with allowlist) and per-tenant egress auditing
- Control plane traffic (versioning, rollouts) must traverse a customer-managed control channel — separate subnets/VPN from inference dataplane
- Support for on-prem private link to our L3 firewall appliance

Could you share an annotated diagram we can circulate to our security/compliance group? A short call to review the diagram would be great; timezones are PT.

Best,
Sofia Martinez
Senior Cloud Architect | Northstar Health

Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment — request for annotated topology and control/data split

Sofia — thanks for the clear requirements and the spreadsheet. Attached is an initial annotated topology (vpc-topology-annotated-v1.png). Notes in the diagram:

1) Control plane: runs in a separate management VPC inside the customer network (customer-owned subnets). Control-plane egress is pinned to an outbound interface using mTLS and customer KMS for key wrapping.
2) Data plane: inference pools run in dedicated private subnets, behind an internal load balancer; traffic between inference nodes and state stores uses an internal service mesh (sidecar) for mutual TLS.
3) Egress: default deny via outbound firewall rules — all allowed egress is documented and routed through the customer perimeter firewall for centralized logging.
4) Audit logs & metrics: control-plane events are forwarded to the customer SIEM via TLS to a collector endpoint; token-level logs are redacted per policy.

Questions for your security team:
- Can we rely on the customer firewall to perform NAT for outbound egress, or do you prefer a managed egress NAT inside the Redwood appliance?
- Do you have a specific KMS API/version we should validate against (your spreadsheet lists a vendor but not API details).

Proposed next step: 45-minute call tomorrow 10:30 PT to walk the diagram and capture redlines. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and a v1->v2 turnaround plan.

Attachments: vpc-topology-annotated-v1.png (png, 820KB)

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Dylan — reviewed v1 and left inline comments below (copied into the body for ease):

1) Control plane path: good to see an explicit management VPC. Please add a note about certificate rotation cadence and whether Redwood supports cert pinning to our CA.
2) Egress NAT: we prefer egress to exit through our perimeter firewall (customer-side NAT) so we keep full egress logging in the chain. Can Redwood support a model where you never perform SNAT to your own IPs?
3) KMS: we use HashiCorp Vault with transit engine (API v1). Need a compatibility check on key wrapping and HSM-backed key policies.
4) Data residency: some inference logs must be held in-region for 90 days — annotate where those logs are stored and the retention configuration.

Also attached a marked-up spreadsheet with additional GK/PCI notes. Can you incorporate these and share v2 before the meeting?

Regards,

Thanks Dylan — reviewed v2 and adding engineering decisions / action items below:

Decisions: 
- Certificate rotation: Redwood supports configurable rotation windows; we will expose an option to accept customer CA root for cert pinning. Ops will require a fingerprint exchange and periodic re-validation (quarterly).
- Egress: we can operate with customer-side NAT only. To preserve health checks and usage telemetry, we will switch to a push-only health callback model where nodes post status to a customer-accepted collector endpoint; no SNAT to Redwood-owned IPs will be performed.
- KMS/Vault Transit: Partner Ops will run a one-time validation using customer's Vault instance (transit v1). We will not store unwrapped keys. HSM-backed policies are compatible; need a runbook step for key rotation.
- Logs/retention: control-plane audit logs will be forwarded to the customer SIEM (in-region) and retained for 90 days; a retention policy will be codified in the template.

Action items (owners & ETA):
1) Dylan: update diagram to show push-only health callbacks + collector endpoint (v2 -> v3) — ETA EOD today.
2) Laura / Partner Ops: schedule Vault transit validation with Northstar — ETA May 28.
3) Hiro / Infra: finalize runbook for CA pinning exchange and key rotation cadence — ETA May 27.
4) Sofia / Northstar: confirm collector endpoint and firewall ACL that allow outbound from inference subnets — ETA May 26.

I'll join the 10:30 PT call and bring the infra runbook draft.
